subject.title: fix(agents): tighten grepSchema context/limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject fractional `grep.context` and `grep.limit` calls even though current sibling tools and upstream Pi still accept numeric values?
rationale: The code change is correct for integer semantics, but choosing a stricter model-facing tool contract and an OpenClaw-specific divergence is a compatibility decision that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Approve targeted integer contract
options.body: Accept the stricter grep schema because both fields represent discrete counts, then rebase and require exact-head checks before merge.

options.title: Align all count fields first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define and implement one coherent integer policy across grep, find, ls, and read count-like parameters.

options.title: Retain upstream numeric compatibility
options.body: Close the PR and keep runtime normalization as the supported behavior for fractional numeric inputs.

recommendation.title: Approve targeted integer contract
recommendation.body: Accept the stricter grep schema because both fields represent discrete counts, then rebase and require exact-head checks before merge.
